sections.text: Substations
Technical Procedure
Introduction

The REL511 is 
a universal line protection, control and monitoring terminal that can be applied to 
transmission and sub-transmission overhead lines and cables in solidly 
earthed, as well as in low resistance earthed networks. The basic 
protection function in REL521 is a full scheme distance protection with indivicual 
measuring elements for the different types of faults that belong to the 
various impedance zones. The terminal includes three impedance measuring zones 
with programmable directionality.

The 
independent measuring elements provide general fault criterion

This procedure
details the steps required to completely check the proper operation and
calibration of the relay. It is recommended this procedure be carried out on an
annually bases. The document is formatted the way to minimize the possibility
of error causing personal injury or damage to equipment.

Safety Precautions

A work permit
must be issued and the qualified maintenance staff should carry the suitable
safety category,

Safety fence
(rope) with caution marks surrounding the work area,
Line isolation and work permit required

Make sure that 
CT secondary circuits are shorted before isolating the current circuits for test 
distance protection

sections.text: Work to be Carried Out

Steps to prepare for relay 
testing

Review technical reference material and 
manufacturer's manual

Obtain copy of relay setting from field 
maintenance file and compare it with the setting on the relay

Obtain outage for line protected by this 
relay

Check that the circuit breaker is opened and 
tagged

Inspect the CT secondary circuits, the V T 
miniature circuit breakers ( mcb.s) and all cabling supplying the relaying

Use the station drawings to isolate the 
following:
 * Breaker trip coils
 * Breaker failure scheme associated with the relay and 
disturbance alarms

sections.text: Testing the relay

items: Carefully follow this test procedure
Verify the test results match the relay setting
Trip the circuit breaker associated with the relay

sections.text: Preparation

items: This procedure shoud be used for performing off load line

Look the EEC panel name plate and check this EEC system designation name plate 
 agrees with the line that has been taken out of service for maintenance

Make sure CT secondary circuits are shorted at the incoming terminal blocks 
 before isolate the relay current circuits for test

sections.text:
Reading the setting from the relay by using 
the PC

items:
By using the six keys on the MMI (mam machine interface) of the relay read the 
 setting

sections.text: Distance protection test

items:
Be sure that the D.C power of the relay is correct by applying a D.C voltmeter 
 across points X16 (17) and X16 (18) on the rear of the relay

Connect the current test leads on the current terminals of the relay 
 X11(1,2,3,8) and the voltage test leads on the voltage terminals of the relay 
 X12 (1,6,8,10)
Connect A.C power to the test set

Inject current, voltage and phase angle by selecting the value of impedance 
 (X)

To test zone (1) phase R to Neutral:
 * Take the value of (X) greater than the maximum value of working for zone 1 
 and decrease it slowly until the 
 relay operates and the Red LED (right) on the MMI be steady light
 * Display the last disturbance on the LCD of the MMI and check the displayed 
 disturbance with the actual fault disturbance
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase S to Neutral
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase T to Neutral
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase R to S
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase S to T
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase T to R
Repeat step 5 to test zone (1) phase R to S To T

sections.text:
Return relay and associated equipment to 
service

items:
Return relay to service by removing the test leads from the relay terminals 
 and the test set
Make sure CT and V T secondary circuits are in normal condition
Remove the disturbance alarm LED`s on the relay which is caused by the test
Request feeder to be returned in service

Take phasor readings of all A C currents and voltages and compare them to 
 those for normal load condition

Check that these reading agree with station meters (MW, MVAR, Amperes and Power 
 Factor)

Place a copy of the test result in 
 the field maintenance file
